checks.s: The deliverable addresses all seven contested terms in this order: (1) Arbitral Institution/Rules, (2) Number of Arbitrators, (3) Seat/Venue, (4) Scope of Arbitrable Claims, (5) Escalation Ladder & Cooling-Off Periods, (6) Interim/Emergency Relief & Injunctive Relief Carve-Outs, and (7) Costs & Fees Allocation.
Each of the seven contested terms includes proposed contract clause language, not merely bullet points or conceptual descriptions.
Each of the seven contested terms is accompanied by a negotiation rationale explaining why the compromise serves both parties' interests.
The Term 1 clause proposes JAMS under the Comprehensive Arbitration Rules as the arbitral institution.
The Term 1 clause does not propose AAA or ICC as the primary institution.
The Term 1 rationale explains JAMS as a bridging or middle-ground option.
The Term 1 rationale references JAMS's cost positioning between AAA (~$19,600 admin fees) and ICC (~$85,000–$120,000 admin fees) for a $17.28M claim.
The Term 1 rationale references at least one of JAMS's domestic reputation or its neutrality.
The Term 2 clause provides for a sole arbitrator below a specified dollar threshold and a three-arbitrator panel at or above that threshold.
The Term 2 clause or rationale references or reconciles the $250,000 small-claims threshold and the $2,500,000 large-claims threshold when explaining the tiered arbitrator structure.
The Term 3 clause proposes Washington, D.C. or a neutral third location other than New York, NY as the seat or venue.
The Term 3 clause does not propose New York, NY as the seat or venue.
The Term 3 rationale addresses geographic and/or legal neutrality considerations for both parties.
The Term 4 clause retains a broad “arising out of or relating to” arbitration scope.
The Term 4 clause does not exclude categories of claims entirely from arbitration.
The Term 4 clause provides for arbitrators with relevant technical or IP expertise for IP infringement or data-breach disputes.
The Term 4 clause allows only narrowly defined injunctive-relief aspects to go to court while keeping damages claims in arbitration.
The Term 5 clause includes mediation as a step in the pre-arbitration escalation process.
The total pre-arbitration escalation period specified in the Term 5 clause is more than 10 days and less than 60 days.
The Term 5 rationale explains how the compressed timelines serve Graystone's desire for efficiency and Meridian's desire for an opportunity to resolve the dispute commercially before arbitration.
The Term 5 clause or rationale addresses Meridian's $25,000 mediation cost cap by adopting it, modifying it, or explicitly discussing it.
The Term 6 clause provides both emergency arbitrator relief and court access for interim injunctive relief.
The Term 6 clause explicitly states that seeking court-ordered interim relief does not waive the right to arbitrate.
The Term 6 clause explicitly states that seeking court-ordered interim relief does not constitute a submission to jurisdiction for purposes other than the interim relief sought.

The Term 7 clause proposes a modified fee-shifting provision, such as a prevailing-party, hybrid/tiered, threshold-triggered, or percentage-limited model, rather than pure loser-pays-all or pure each-bears-own.
The Term 7 rationale addresses Meridian's concern about disproportionate risk exposure as the smaller-revenue party and Graystone's objective of deterring frivolous claims.

The proposed language for all seven terms is drafted as operative contract provisions suitable for insertion into the MSA, rather than primarily as bullet points, summaries, or conceptual descriptions.
The clause language is consistent with the agreed governing law of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles, as stated in Section 14.1.
The deliverable references MSA Internal Reference No. GCP-MAS-2025-0041 or correctly identifies both Graystone Capital Partners, LLC and Meridian Advanced Systems, Inc.
The negotiation rationale for each of the seven compromise terms explains how the proposed language serves both Graystone's and Meridian's interests.
The rationales reference Graystone's regulatory exposure and cost-efficiency concerns as a regulated financial services firm.
The rationales reference Meridian's proprietary technology protection concerns and smaller-revenue-base risk.
Any TCV figure stated is $43,200,000 or $43.2M.
Any ACV figure stated is $8,640,000 or $8.64M.
Any general liability cap figure stated is $17,280,000 or $17.28M, identified as 2× ACV where that relationship is stated.
Any monthly run rate figure stated is $720,000.

Any claim-value thresholds used in the tiered arbitrator provision or escalation ladder are internally consistent with the MSA financial parameters and reference or are reconcilable with the $250,000 small-claims and $2,500,000 large-claims thresholds from the drafts.
No claim-value threshold used in the tiered arbitrator provision or escalation ladder exceeds the $17.28M liability cap.

The deliverable discloses Graystone's internal authority limits, walk-away positions, board authorization details, or the playbook's classification as “Attorney-Client Privileged & Confidential — Work Product.”

The deliverable reads as an internal strategy memo, work-product analysis, or privileged communication rather than an external-facing proposal for the June 23, 2025 facilitated negotiation session with counterparty counsel.
The Term 5 clause specifies a concrete number of days for each escalation step.
The Term 5 clause or rationale states who bears the mediator's fees.
The rationale states AAA admin fees as approximately $19,600 for a $17.28M claim.
The rationale states ICC admin fees as approximately $85,000–$120,000 for a $17.28M claim.
The rationale states sole arbitrator total estimated fees as approximately $65,000, based on 10 days × $6,500/day.
The rationale states three-arbitrator panel total estimated fees as approximately $195,000, based on 10 days × $19,500/day.
The rationale uses cost comparison figures to justify the compromise position on the arbitral institution in Term 1.
The rationale uses cost comparison figures to justify the compromise position on arbitrator count in Term 2.
The compromise clause language includes a provision requiring arbitration proceedings, evidence, and awards to be kept confidential.
The Term 2 clause provides an expedited sole-arbitrator procedure for disputes under the $250,000 small-claims threshold.
The deliverable explicitly proposes uncapped liability for data-breach/IP claims.

The Term 4 clause or rationale acknowledges the dispute between Graystone's uncapped position and Meridian's proposed 3× ACV ($25,920,000 or $25.92M) cap for data-breach/IP indemnity in the context of the scope or carve-out discussion.

Each compromise clause fits within the existing Article XIV Sections 14.1 through 14.9 numbering—14.1 Governing Law, 14.2 Escalation, 14.3 Institution/Rules, 14.4 Arbitrators, 14.5 Seat/Venue, 14.6 Scope, 14.7 Interim Relief, 14.8 Costs/Fees, and 14.9 Miscellaneous—or clearly indicates where new subsections are added.
